messages.author: e63f32a7ce6b8890
messages.subject: Check installed version of rApache
parts:
I am working on automating the installation of rApache (using Chef).  One thing I need to do is skip the compilation and installation if the version of rApache I want is already installed.  Is there a way to tell which version of rApache is installed?

The options I see are:
1) Check if mod_R.so exists.  This allows me to skip installation if rApache is already installed, but it does not support upgrading rApache if the installed version is old.
2) Add an r-info url and check that.  However, this requires r-info to be running, which we may not want in production.  It also requires httpd to be running which may not be the case while the server is being provisioned.
3) After installing rApache, write a metadata file with the version installed.

Is there a more standard way of checking the version of rApache?  I tried using `nm mod_R.so` and `objdump -x mod_R.so` but I did not see anything I could use.

Thanks

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: Check installed version of rApache
parts:
The github repo contains a debian dir with the required files. You can build the package on Debian/Ubuntu by running

debuild -us -uc

Alternatively, you can grab binaries for Ubuntu 12.04 and up from launchpad:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:opencpu/rapache
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libapache2-mod-r-base

Last time I checked RHEL doesn't seem to support R (which is a quite important dependency), at least it's not in their repos. You can grab it from EPEL or so, but there is no guarantee that it will work with the versions of the dependencies that ship with RHEL. I've had some bad experiences that were due to Cairo on RHEL being wayyy outdated and decided it was not worth it.

Thanks Jeroen!

In case anyone is interested I have rApache successfully running on RHEL6 x86_64 with R 3.0.1. I installed R-core, R-devel, httpd-devel, texinfo, and libapreq2 from EPEL.  I had to install libjpeg-turbo (required by R-core) and texinfo-tex (required by R-devel) using CentOS RPMs.  From there, the source install instructions work fine.

So it looks like the best solution for us would be to create an RPM for rapache and install it into our custom repo.
